 ‘Wish we could have got to it’: 17 victims in crime spree that left three stabbed in Topeka 
 Ron Hubbard said he was hanging with a friend Wednesday, Oct. 28, when they noticed something unusual. By Daesha Gear Published : Oct. 29, 2026 at 6:41 PM CDT | Updated : 17 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google TOPEKA, Kan. (WIBW) - Ron Hubbard never expected fiction to become reality.
 ​“I was thinking about a scenario I seen on TV where a delivery guy did the same when the police was chasing a guy who stole a car,” Hubbard said.
 ​Hubbard said he was hanging with a friend Wednesday, Oct. 28, when they noticed something unusual.
 ​“I happened to look up the street to my left, and I seen this strange guy,” Hubbard said.
 ​The man, now identified as Adam Schwegman , also caught another bystander’s attention.
 ​“We confronted him because the other guy had been up at the park, where this all took place,” Hubbard said.
 ​Topeka police say, an hour earlier, Schwegman stabbed two people in the 1600 block of S.W. Fillmore. His booking charges also include an allegation of rape at that address .
 ​TPD says Schwegman then moved into the 1400 and 1500 block of Fillmore, breaking into two homes -- four children were inside one of them, including a four-month-old. Officials say they were not hurt.
 ​However, it didn’t stop there.
 ​Police say a third victim was stabbed in the 600 block of S.W. 3rd St.
 ​And finally, a 70-year-old woman was hurt when Schwegman attacked her at Ward Meade Park. Schwegman was running from there when Hubbard spotted him.
 ​“I decided to step in, throw my leg out, trip him and he landed over here in the grass, and the knife fell in the grass,” Hubbard said. 
 ​Hubbard tells 13 NEWS he kicked the knife to the sidewalk, as the second person held Schwegman. He got away, but police soon caught him.
 ​Schwegman was booked in connection with 16 charges, including aggravated battery and rape.
 ​Hubbard says he was glad to step in to prevent further harm.
 ​“Well, if you see something bad, try to help stop it. I wish we could have got to it before this happened,” Hubbard said. 
 ​Schwegman made his first appearance in court on Thursday, Oct. 29. The judge has set a total bond of $3 million.
